data.title: Bajaj Housing Finance Q2 Profit Rises 18% To Rs 757 Cr, AUM Grows 25%
data.description:
Housing finance company reports 18.3 per cent growth in total income to Rs 3,251 crore in Q2 FY27, while net interest income rises 10 per cent year-on-year

Bajaj Housing Finance reported an 18 per cent year-on-year increase in profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 757 crore for the second quarter of FY27, supported by growth in total income and assets under management (AUM).

The housing finance company had reported a profit after tax of Rs 643 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. Total income increased 18.3 per cent to Rs 3,251 crore in the July-September quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 2,748 crore in the year-ago period, according to a regulatory filing.

Net interest income (NII), which represents the difference between interest earned and interest expended, rose 10 per cent to Rs 1,055 crore during the quarter, against Rs 956 crore in Q2 FY26.

Assets Under Management Rise 25 Per Cent

Bajaj Housing Finance's assets under management grew 25 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1.58 lakh crore as of September 30, 2026, compared with Rs 1.27 lakh crore a year earlier.

The growth reflects an expansion in the company's lending portfolio during the quarter, with AUM crossing Rs 1.5 lakh crore.

Meanwhile, loan losses and provisions declined to Rs 35 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 43 crore in the corresponding period last year, indicating a reduction in the amount set aside against potential credit losses.

The September-quarter performance reflects continued growth in the company's earnings and managed assets, alongside lower loan-loss provisions.

data.title: Festive Housing Demand Turns Selective As Buyers Seek Value
data.description:
July-September sales point to resilient housing demand, but changing buyer preferences, premiumisation and affordability are reshaping festive-season purchases

India’s housing market is heading into the festive season with demand holding firm, but homebuyers are becoming more discerning about where and what they buy. Developer credibility, location, construction quality, connectivity and long-term value are increasingly shaping purchase decisions, signalling a shift from buying on festive sentiment alone to making more considered investments in residential property.

According to Anarock Research, housing sales across the top seven cities rose 3 per cent year-on-year to 1,00,220 units in July-September 2026, while sales value increased 2 per cent to Rs 1.55 lakh crore. Average residential prices climbed 7 per cent to Rs 9,714 per sq ft.

Are Buyers Returning With More Conviction?

The modest sales growth does not by itself capture the changing behaviour of buyers entering the festive market. Developers are seeing customers who are more willing to purchase, but are taking greater care over the developer, location and long-term usefulness of the property.

Ravi Agarwal, Chairman and Managing Director, Lloyds Realty Developers Ltd., said the recent improvement should not be interpreted as a sharp festive surge. According to him, buyers who had postponed purchases are returning as confidence stabilises, particularly in established Mumbai neighbourhoods where they can upgrade without leaving familiar locations.

“It’s mostly underlying demand, with festive timing adding a lift. A 3 per cent rise is too modest to call a festive surge,” Agarwal said. He added that the quarter after Diwali would provide a clearer indication of whether the recovery is structural, with redevelopment benefiting from demand for better homes in established localities.

Pradeep Aggarwal, Founder and Chairman, Signature Global (India) Ltd., sees stronger end-user fundamentals behind the current market. He said improved income visibility and a growing preference for home ownership among young professionals are supporting purchase decisions, particularly among buyers looking for credible developers.

“The foundation is also end-user driven, supported by improved income visibility and a growing preference for home ownership among young professionals,” Aggarwal said. He added that buyers in the NCR are increasingly choosing developers with strong delivery records, while micro-markets such as Southern Peripheral Road, Dwarka Expressway, Sohna and Gurugram West are attracting demand.

What Are Buyers Actually Paying For?

The changing buyer is perhaps most visible in the premium segment, where purchasing decisions are increasingly moving beyond headline price and apartment size. Buyers are assessing the experience a property offers and whether its design, location and execution justify the overall cost.

Sidharth Chowdhry, Managing Director, Dalcore, said luxury buyers are becoming more informed and are placing greater emphasis on the character and quality of a residence. Architecture, privacy, functionality and craftsmanship are emerging as differentiators as buyers look beyond conventional amenity packages.

“Today’s luxury homebuyer is increasingly informed and selective, placing greater emphasis on the quality and character of a residence rather than price or size alone,” Chowdhry said. He added that developers need to respond with homes reflecting architectural intent, thoughtful use of space and craftsmanship rather than relying on standardised luxury features.

Himanshu Luthra, Managing Director, Divine Vision Infra, said the same scrutiny is extending beyond the luxury segment. Buyers are increasingly assessing whether a property makes practical and financial sense over the long term, with location and connectivity becoming important alongside documentation and construction quality.

“Buyers want a good location, good connectivity, clear legal papers and long-term worth before they buy,” Luthra said. He added that festive sentiment may accelerate decisions, but sustained demand will depend on genuine end-user interest and confidence in the project and its developer.

Is Premiumisation Changing The Shape Of Demand?

The shift towards higher-value homes is visible in the market data, but it also raises questions about who is being left behind. Knight Frank’s January-September 2026 data shows homes priced above Rs 1 crore accounted for 55 per cent of sales, up from 50 per cent a year earlier.

Shekhar Patel, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Ganesh Housing Ltd. and National President of CREDAI, said premiumisation should not automatically be read as a wholesale shift towards luxury housing. Rising land and construction costs are pushing reasonably sized homes beyond the existing affordable-housing threshold.

“Premiumization is partly a classification problem,” Patel said, pointing to the Rs 45 lakh affordable housing cap, which has remained unchanged since 2017. He added that demand for 60–90 sq m homes remains resilient, particularly in Ahmedabad, suggesting that affordability constraints are partly being created by the way housing categories are defined.

Ankita Luharuka, CEO, Alliance City Developers, said premiumisation is also forcing developers to rethink how products are planned for different buyer groups. The objective, she said, should be to provide the right combination of configuration, space, amenities and connectivity without pushing the overall purchase cost beyond the target customer’s reach.

“Developers need to adopt a more differentiated approach to product planning,” Luharuka said. She added that pricing should reflect local market conditions and project value, while milestone-linked payment plans and structured buying options can help customers manage cash flows without relying on large discounts.

The festive season is therefore revealing a housing market where demand is not simply returning in greater volume, but becoming more considered in quality. Buyers are weighing credibility, location, design, affordability and long-term value more closely, forcing developers to compete on relevance rather than festive incentives alone.

data.title: IIFCL, Two Coal India Units Eye FY27 Listings, DIPAM Chief Says
data.description:
Mahanadi Coalfields has filed its draft IPO prospectus, while the government is preparing India Infrastructure Finance Company and South Eastern Coalfields for listing in the current financial year

The Centre is targeting stock market listings for India Infrastructure Finance Company (IIFCL) and two Coal India subsidiaries, Mahanadi Coalfields (MCL) and South Eastern Coalfields (SECL), in FY27, Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) Secretary Arunish Chawla said, according to media reports.

The planned listings follow the stock market debuts of Coal India subsidiaries BCCL in January 2026 and CMPDI in March 2026.

IPO Preparations Under Way

The government has begun preparations for IIFCL’s initial public offering, inviting bids to appoint a registrar and share transfer agent, as well as an advertising agency for the proposed issue. Eligible bidders can submit applications online until November 3, according to the report. MCL has already filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP), while SECL is also slated for listing during the financial year.

The three offerings will have different implications for government receipts. Proceeds from IIFCL’s IPO will accrue directly to the Centre, its sole shareholder. Proceeds from stake sales in MCL and SECL will go to Coal India, their parent company, with the government potentially benefiting indirectly through dividends in FY28.

IIFCL’s Financial Performance

Wholly owned by the Centre, IIFCL was established in 2006 to provide long-term financial assistance to viable infrastructure projects. It registered with the Reserve Bank of India as an infrastructure finance non-banking financial company in 2013. The company had a net worth of Rs 17,898 crore at the end of FY26. Its net profit fell 36 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,379 crore in FY26, weighed down by mark-to-market losses on offshore borrowings amid foreign exchange fluctuations.

Coal India Units’ Production And Profits

MCL was Coal India’s largest-producing subsidiary in FY26, with output of 218.31 million tonnes and net profit of Rs 10,698 crore. SECL produced 176.29 million tonnes during the year and reported net profit of Rs 4,755 crore. Coal India’s total production declined to 768.19 million tonnes in FY26 from 781.06 million tonnes a year earlier. Its consolidated profit after tax fell to Rs 31,071 crore from Rs 35,450 crore, while revenue from operations was broadly stable at Rs 1,68,400 crore, compared with Rs 1,69,177 crore in FY25.

Government Disinvestment Target

The proposed listings form part of the Centre’s broader disinvestment and asset monetisation programme. The government has raised Rs 62,124 crore in FY27 so far and has effectively met its Rs 80,000 crore target for miscellaneous capital receipts after including around Rs 26,500 crore expected from the strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank, which is nearing completion. The planned offerings would mark a resumption of government IPOs after more than two years. The last such offering was the Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (IREDA) IPO in FY24, when the government sold a 10 per cent stake.

data.title: Reliance Says Jio Satellite Services Also Await India Clearances
data.description:
Reliance Industries responds to Elon Musk’s criticism of Starlink’s delayed India entry, saying Jio’s satellite services are also awaiting government approvals and all applicants must follow the same rules

Reliance Industries on Friday, 16 October, said its Jio satellite services were still awaiting government clearances, responding to Elon Musk’s allegations that powerful business interests were impeding Starlink’s entry into India. The company said domestic and foreign applicants must follow the same regulatory process.

The exchange brings the regulatory hurdles facing satellite broadband operators into focus as Elon Musk’s Starlink seeks to enter India’s internet market, where Reliance Jio is an established telecom player. Reliance said it welcomed competition, including from Starlink, and cited Jio’s growth since its commercial entry into India’s telecom market in 2016.

Reliance Says All Applicants Must Follow The Same Rules

In a statement posted on X, Reliance said India welcomed investment and innovation from domestic and international companies, provided they operated within the law. It said the government had stated that the same process applied to every applicant, irrespective of whether the company was Indian or foreign. “Jio’s own satellite services await clearances,” Reliance said, adding that it had never feared competition and viewed it as a test of which company served customers better. The statement did not identify each pending approval or specify a launch date for Jio’s satellite services.

Musk Accuses Powerful Business Interests Of Blocking Starlink

The response followed a series of social media posts by Musk, the chief executive of SpaceX, which operates Starlink. Musk alleged that powerful business interests were blocking the satellite internet service’s entry into India to protect existing market positions. He also addressed Reliance chairman Mukesh Ambani sarcastically as “Prime Minister Ambani” in a post seeking access to the Indian market.

Starlink’s proposed entry has drawn attention because satellite broadband could expand internet access in areas where conventional connectivity is limited. Musk has argued that the service could help connect underserved communities, while the Indian government has maintained that operators must satisfy the applicable regulatory and security requirements before beginning commercial operations.

Jio Cites 530 Million Customers Since 2016 Entry

Reliance also pointed to Jio’s record in the telecom market as evidence of its approach to competition. The company said Jio entered India’s crowded telecom sector in 2016 with no customers and had built a base of more than 530 million customers over the following decade. The statement did not provide a specific timeline for the launch of Jio’s satellite internet services. Its response focused on equal treatment of applicants, compliance with Indian laws, and the company’s stated willingness to compete with international operators.

data.title: Diesel Sales Jump 25% As Festive Demand Lifts Fuel Use
data.description:
State-run fuel retailers sold 3.65 million tonnes in the first half of October as festival-linked transport demand, agricultural use and lower pump prices boosted diesel purchases

Diesel sales surged 25.4 per cent year-on-year in the first half of October, as festive-season transport activity and agricultural demand lifted fuel consumption, preliminary industry data showed on Friday. State-run oil marketing companies sold 3.65 million tonnes of diesel during 1 to 15 October, with purchases also supported by lower retail prices than those offered by private fuel retailers.

The increase comes as global diesel prices climb amid supply disruptions linked to the Iran war and the Russia-Ukraine conflict. While state-run retailers have kept pump prices unchanged since May, private operators have raised prices and redirected fuel towards export markets, creating a price gap that is drawing customers towards public-sector outlets.

Festive Transport And Agricultural Demand Support Sales

Diesel demand has benefited from increased trucking during the festival season, as wholesalers build inventories ahead of Diwali in November. SP Singh, a senior fellow at the Indian Foundation of Transport Research and Training, attributed the rise to stronger agricultural demand and higher transportation activity. Farmers also use diesel-powered generator sets for irrigation, adding to consumption.

Truck sales provide another indicator of stronger transport activity. Sales rose to 44,323 units in September, an increase of 33.57 per cent from August, according to Singh. Wholesalers' inventory-building ahead of the festival period has contributed to higher trucking activity, he said.

State-Run Retailers Gain From Price Gap

Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation have kept retail fuel prices unchanged since May, despite higher global fuel prices. The three state-run companies are absorbing losses of around Rs 20 per litre on diesel sales, according to Prashant Vasisht, senior vice-president at rating agency ICRA.

Private retailers Nayara Energy and Reliance Industries have raised fuel prices and are exporting products to benefit from stronger international margins. Diesel at private fuel stations is around Rs 5 per litre costlier than at state-run outlets, while petrol is Rs 3 per litre more expensive, according to the report. The price differential has encouraged some customers to switch to public-sector retailers.

Gasoline Sales Also Edge Higher

State-run retailers' gasoline sales rose to 1.55 million tonnes during 1 to 15 October, up 0.9 per cent from the same period in September. The increase was considerably smaller than the growth recorded in diesel sales over the same period.

Diesel is also being used to generate electricity amid rising power demand, Vasisht said. The latest sales figures reflect the combined impact of seasonal consumption, agricultural requirements and the shift towards state-run outlets offering lower retail prices.

data.title: Motorola’s Signature 27 Is An All-out Flagship Bet In A Shrinking Market, Says Shivam Ranjan
data.description:
Motorola’s APAC Marketing Head sheds light on memory-led price inflation, Lenovo’s supply-chain advantage and why seven years of updates is now hygiene for flagship buyers

India’s smartphone market is going through one of its toughest stretches in years. Shipments fell 10 per cent year-on-year in the April to June quarter of 2026, the steepest June-quarter decline in six years, with soaring memory costs pushing up prices across nearly every segment and leading many buyers to delay upgrades. The entry-level segment took the biggest hit, while vivo held the top spot with an 18 per cent share.

The slide began earlier. In Q1, shipments fell 3 per cent, the weakest quarter in six years, and more than 80 models saw average price hikes of 15 per cent. Counterpoint now expects the market to shrink by 13 per cent over the full year, with manufacturers leaning on premium devices, financing offers and portfolio changes until component costs ease.

Premium is the one pocket holding up. That makes this a telling moment for flagship silicon. At Snapdragon Summit 2026, Qualcomm unveiled the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and a higher-end Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, both built on a 2nm process. Both chips reach clock speeds of up to 5GHz, and the Extreme variant gets the bigger AI leap, with a 35 per cent gain over the Gen 5 against 14 per cent for the standard chip. Xiaomi and Motorola were the first to show phones powered by the new chips at the event.

Motorola’s entry is the Signature 27, built around the Extreme chip and pitched as the company’s most ambitious phone yet. On the sidelines of India Mobile Congress 2026, where the Signature 27 was shown to India, we spoke to Shivam Ranjan, APAC Marketing Head, Motorola Mobility. We covered what makes the phone stand out, how Motorola is handling the memory crunch, who the buyer is, and why software support has become table stakes.

Here are the edited excerpts:

Tell us about the new phone. What makes the Signature 27 stand out?

While we have not formally announced the phone globally yet, that will happen soon, within 2026, for both India and the world. We are here to support our partner Qualcomm, which is announcing its latest chipsets, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and the 8 Elite. This will be one of the first phones globally to come with the Extreme Gen 6, so we are here to share a few glimpses.

The first reason it stands out is that we have been making mobile phones since 1973, and we can comfortably say this is the best phone we have ever made. That is not just about performance. It cuts across the device, including imaging. We redefined imaging when we introduced the Signature last year, and this year we are taking it a notch higher with the latest camera technology and Qualcomm’s chipset.

On agentic capabilities, taking consumer intent to action, this device will bring use cases that today are truly imaginary. You will see incredible performance, gaming and connectivity. With six antennas, you get breakthrough connectivity, and download speeds go up by more than 25 per cent, which also helps cloud AI models and your overall agentic AI experience.

On software, there is a promise of seven years of OS upgrades and security patches. All of this comes with a redesigned language: an aluminium silhouette with curved contours, with ceramic and brushed aluminium, and a completely differentiated camera module. This is the best of what you can do with a smartphone.

Memory-led inflation has pushed up smartphone prices globally, and TSMC is raising chip manufacturing prices too. How does the market evolve, and how does India adapt?

This is a category-wide issue, not limited to any geography. It comes from the AI boom, with demand outstripping the supply of memory, and other components are seeing an impact too. Everyone in the industry feels it.

But Motorola is far better equipped than some other OEMs to manage this, because of the might of the Lenovo ecosystem. Lenovo is the number one PC manufacturer, so our supply chain and procurement are in a far better position to secure what is needed for each market, including India.

The markets will keep evolving. We are seeing an impact, and volumes are shrinking. But the adaptation we are seeing is a premium movement. Consumers are moving up the price ladder because they pay for products where they see value, not necessarily to hit a particular price point.

When you say you are well equipped, do you mean you accept that prices will stay high, or that you will wait it out until they come down?

There is no question of waiting it out. What I mean is that our parent company is the largest PC manufacturer in the world, so we are well equipped to secure supplies for our products, including Motorola. There is no concern that we will not have enough supply in the market. We are well positioned to handle the situation.

It is also not something any single OEM can change. We are here to stay and to participate in the market, and there is no question of pausing. You can see that with the Signature 27 and the other products you will see soon. What we can assure consumers is that we will stay competitive and give them more value where it is required. That is how we differentiate.

Who is the buyer for this phone? The first Signature was one of the best phones of the year and came in under Rs 60,000. Rumours put this one at around Rs 90,000.

I won’t comment on pricing. But last year’s Signature was our first attempt at a candy bar flagship, and we deliberately kept it at entry-flagship price points because we first needed to gain acceptance in that segment.

With the Signature 27, we have gone for an all-out flagship. It is the Ultra when it comes to everything. It has things you do not see with other brands, such as Bang & Olufsen audio, exclusive to us on this device. The design language is innovative, and the chipset, camera, and agentic experiences are the latest and the greatest. We kept what people liked about the first Signature. When we introduced it, one of the questions you had was why we did not go for the Elite chipset. We have addressed that with this one, for people who wanted the best of the best.

The buyer is someone who wants to challenge the status quo and ask why they should keep buying the same brands. That is a tech-first buyer, an early adopter and an innovation enthusiast, someone who is design-first too, but truly a flagship buyer.

Is it safe to say you are done with the affordable flagship segment?

I wouldn’t say that. We are not giving up any segment. Our attempt is to offer consumers a viable option at every price point, and last year’s Signature played the affordable flagship role for us.

As we move along, that role may be filled by a product from another franchise, or by a product within the Signature franchise. Last year’s Signature also has time to go. We do not plan to end it soon, and as you said yourself, you still love the product. It is extremely competitive, and there is a segment of buyers looking for an affordable or entry-level flagship. We let that product play that game.

You are offering seven years of OS updates. Is that a primary concern for Indian buyers?

With flagship devices, consumers now take this as hygiene. They want a worry-free, peace-of-mind experience for as long as they plan to keep the phone. It will not necessarily get you higher sales, but if you do not offer it, you create question marks.

It is a need-to-have to cut ice with this cohort. If you do not have it, you do not even cross the threshold. If you do have it, you do not get an additional premium for it. So we are making sure we give what a flagship consumer asks for and deserves.

data.title: Mahindra Group Appoints Fritz Fernandes To Lead Events & Partnerships At Mahindra Experiences
data.description:
Fernandes brings over 17 years of experience across luxury lifestyle, hospitality, music, sports and cinema, with a focus on business development and consumer experiences

Fritz Fernandes has joined Mahindra Group as Head of Events and Partnerships for Mahindra Experiences. He shared the career update in a LinkedIn post.

Fernandes brings over 17 years of experience across luxury lifestyle, hospitality, music, sports and cinema, with a focus on building businesses and consumer experiences.

Before joining Mahindra Group, Fernandes was Vice-President and Head of Experiences at PVR Limited.

Over the course of his career, he has also held roles at The Bay Club-Mumbai, Cadila Pharmaceuticals, Condé Nast India, Football Sports Development Limited, DNA Networks and EMI Music.
